Today's verdict BEARISH-DEFENSIVE
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 1/10: price action is calm, only 1-2 signals lit vs VIX Spike Tier 1/4 BROAD with skew active and 50% probability: options market is pricing a vol expansion event
Price hasn't moved but dealers are charging up for protection via elevated put demand. These are not the same signal. The options market leads price. Trust skew here as the early indicator: calm crash index means the event hasn't happened, not that it won't.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score 70/100: STRONG BUY, capitulation regime vs Divergence composite ELEVATED: 19 bearish pairs vs 4 bullish, net bias 15 bearish out of 40 pairs
Sentiment marks a buy precisely when the internal structure is the most bearish-skewed it can get. Contrarian scores can mark lows, but divergence at this scale precedes price weakness. Trust the divergence composite: it reflects what assets are doing, not how participants feel.
Today's tension
Sentiment signals a capitulation buy while cross-asset internals are fracturing at the broadest level in months.
Bull
The contrarian score at **70** reads a capitulation regime, the strongest buy setup in the system. Zero active confluences and a Tier **1/4** VIX signal with no backwardation mean no compounding stress event is building yet.
Bear
**57.5%** of tracked pairs are diverging, with **19** bearish setups against only **4** bullish out of **40** pairs. The macro regime is TRANSITIONAL at just **25%** confidence, meaning the system cannot identify a clean directional state.
The tell: Watch the SMH/SPY correlation, which has moved from **+0.55** to **-0.43**. Semiconductors recoupling with the broad market is the first confirmation that the buy signal has structural support.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The regime score says STABLE, the crash index reads 1/10, and the contrarian sits at 70. On those three inputs alone you'd lean long into weakness. The problem is the fourth input: 57.5% of cross-asset pairs are diverging with 19 bearish setups against 4 bullish. That is not noise. A divergence composite at the maximum score of 100 with a risk-off bias carrying 3 aligned signals is a market where the index holds while the internals quietly break.

For positioning, the split between NDX up 1.2% and RUT down -0.6% over five days is the visible expression of what the divergence data is showing. Capital is concentrating in the largest, most liquid names and leaking out of everything cyclical and small. KRE vs XLF correlation has swung to -0.58 from +0.16: regional banks are not part of the financials rally, they are trading a separate stress story. SPHB vs SPLV collapsed from +0.85 to +0.22, meaning high-beta and low-vol have stopped moving together, which is almost always a sign that the market is beginning to price a specific risk rather than moving on macro liquidity. You size exposures to the rotation, not the index level.

The contrarian STRONG BUY is real but contingent on the TRANSITIONAL macro regime resolving upward, and confidence there is only 25%. The reading that flips the stance defensively is VIX backwardation activating: all three tracked confluences require it, none are live today, and the moment one fires, the skew signal and the divergence composite combine into a compounding stress event that the calm crash index will not survive.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

TRANSITIONAL at 25% confidence is the lowest-conviction reading this system can produce without calling a clean state. It means the macro backdrop is shifting but the direction is not yet determined.

The regime state labels as STABLE because no break has occurred, but the risk-off bias carries 3 aligned signals. These readings are compatible: STABLE means no rupture yet, risk-off bias means the balance of evidence is leaning defensive.

At 25% confidence, you position for range, not trend. Scaling into single-directional bets in either direction is the error.

The contrarian STRONG BUY at 70 argues for adding on weakness, but in a TRANSITIONAL regime with explicit risk-off bias, that exposure belongs against defined levels where you can observe whether the macro regime is resolving bullish or bearish.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means that asset pairs which historically moved together have stopped doing so. Correlation drift is the size of that break, measured as a shift in the co-movement coefficient.

Today's composite sits in the ELEVATED zone: 57.5% of 40 tracked pairs are actively diverging, with 19 tilted bearish and 4 bullish. The Mother Jaws score is at its ceiling, 100.

Six specific pairs are in DEEP DIVERGENCE (score 80 each). The vix_move pair has surged from +0.22 to +0.79: equity volatility and rate volatility are now moving in lockstep, a coupling that historically precedes credit spread widening because it signals that the two major risk-pricing markets are seeing the same thing.

SMH vs SPY has flipped from +0.55 to -0.43: semiconductors are no longer a read-through for the broad market. The SPHB/SPLV pair (high-beta vs low-volatility stocks) dropped from +0.85 to +0.22: these two used to move almost identically, now they're splitting, which means the market is repricing beta specifically.

Visa vs Mastercard drifted to -0.68 from +0.53: two businesses with nearly identical models are diverging, which points to something idiosyncratic within payments or financials broadly. KRE vs XLF hit -0.58 from +0.16: regional bank stress is decoupling from the broader financial sector.

When six foundational pairs break simultaneously, the index level is a misleading summary of what is actually happening underneath.

Confluences — most proven alpha of the framework 0/3 ACTIVE
AI read · what the confluences mean now

Zero of the three tracked cross-signal confluences are active. All three require VIX backwardation as a prerequisite, and backwardation is not present.

That absence matters in both directions. It means no compounding stress event is firing today: credit stress, small-cap drawdown, and yen safe-haven flow are not amplifying each other into a single forcing mechanism.

The options market is pricing risk (skew active, 50% vol-expansion probability) but has not yet moved into the term structure shape that defines a compound event. You're positioned in a window where the divergence picture is bearish but the cross-signal amplifiers are quiet.

The moment backwardation activates, all three confluences become immediate candidates, and the character of the market shifts from internal stress to systemic pricing.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Asia is uniformly weak over the five-day window. Shanghai Composite is the regional leader and it is down 1.5%.

KOSPI is the laggard at -4.7%, a level of underperformance that points to Korea-specific pressure, consistent with the semiconductor divergence visible in the SMH/SPY pair. Europe is split along defensive lines: the Swiss SMI leads at +0.5% while EuroStoxx 50 slips -0.7%, a defensive tilt within the region given Switzerland's heavy pharma and consumer staples weighting.

The US mirrors the global pattern internally: NDX leads at +1.2%, Russell 2000 drags at -0.6%, extending the large-cap concentration trade. Crypto confirms the risk-off lean: SOL is the best of a poor week at -0.3%, ETH the worst at -3.2%.

The cross-region read is consistent everywhere you look: cyclical, small-cap, and high-beta assets are losing ground, while mega-cap and defensive pockets are holding. That pattern supports the NDX/RUT split continuing into the US session until Asia stabilizes.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

A crash index at 1/10 and a VIX Spike Detector at Tier 1/4 are measuring different markets. The crash index tracks realized conditions: price drawdowns, breadth deterioration, credit stress.

One signal is lit, the rest are quiet. The VIX Spike Detector reads the options market's forward pricing: skew is active, vol-expansion probability sits at 50%, meaning dealers are treating the next move as a coin flip between calm and vol expansion.

Backwardation is not present, which keeps the signal at its lowest tier rather than escalating. This is a coherent state.

Price can be quiet while the options market builds protection for a move that has not happened yet. The divergence to track: if the crash index climbs past 3 while skew stays active, that is the options market being right before price confirms it.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
